# Additive tuning of 2026-11-02, base re-measure of scenario 1

## Run identity


**This line is the `base` stage of round 1 of the engine layer, measured again, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1877](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877) asked for.** It replaces [the first measurement of the base](additive-tuning-of-2026-10-31-base-re-measure-of-scenario-1.md), which passed 58 of 153. The owner voided that measurement [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6568926331), because its oracles graded a tree that missed the files a session deleted or moved through the shell. [#1923](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1923) fixed the grading tree, and this line measures scenario 1, the documents alone, again with the fixed grader. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-1 tuning`. It is the `scenario-1` arm of the additive tier over the 22 probes of the tuning set, at 7 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288.

**One tree, two pins, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The canary of 8 sessions held 4 records that named paths outside the workspace: each searched the whole disk for an overlay file, a built engine or a decision record, and the sandbox binds none of those paths. The owner read them and [passed the canary](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6570755820). The driver halted at 114 of 154 sessions, because the recorder of `L1-additive-scenario-1-p1-r3` exited 5. `tools/probe/probe-transform.sh` made a directory named after the top-level file `DEVELOPING.md`, so it could not copy that file into the oracle tree. [#1925](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1925) fixed the recorder.

**The pin moved once.** The first 114 sessions recorded at `335b2d6d`. Then `campaign.sh --repin` moved the batch's pin to `b85f1704`, the commit of #1925 on `main`. It moved the pin only after it showed that the engine binary, the plan identity of the line and the task of every probe were the same at both commits. The batch's `pins` file holds the move. The driver then continued in the same try root at `b85f1704`, with every other argument of its first launch. It drew `p1-r3` again, and that session recorded at the new pin. The driver halted once more at 145 of 154, when the harness of one session failed. It ran that session again and finished. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 154 sessions and cost 11999 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 1 stopped at the turn cap, 0 stopped at the session budget, 114 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 1 passed 81 of the 154 sessions it graded, 53%. The voided measurement passed 58 of 153, 38%, at the same count over the same 22 probes. The difference comes from the grader: the voided line graded a tree without the changes a session made through the shell. The base row compares this measurement with the screening measurement of scenario 1 on 2026-10-18, which passed 39 of 72 in [the screening transcript](additive-screening-of-2026-10-18-scenario-1.md). The difference is -1.6 points, with the interval [-15.1, +12.2]. The two measurements do not share a probe, so the row compares two different task sets. The keep rule does not read a base, and a base is never kept. `try.sh result` wrote `1 b85f1704` to the base pin, and a confirmation of the engine layer reads that pin.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 15000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 12436 cents against its cap, and the 154 recorded sessions account for 11999 cents of that sum. The difference is the sessions that recorded nothing: the three harness failures and the recorder failure before the first halt, and the one harness failure before the second halt.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1877/base-2/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.

```yaml
      argument: "{\"description\":\"Find how corpus records undeclared evidence citations\",\"subagent_type\":\"Explore\",\"prompt\":\"This is a documentation corpus (Headwater project) with a convention where documents have YAML front matter with a `relations.cites_evidence` list, and the body text sometimes contains inline links like `([evaluation](../evaluations/some-file.md))` that point to evaluation documents. Also check if there's a registry file (search for \\\"HW-REG-\\\" prefixed IDs, maybe docs/registries or similar) that tracks evidence links or citation issues across the corpus.\\n\\nPlease:\\n1. Search docs/obligations/*.md for existing records about undeclared citations, undeclared evidence_basis, or front-matter vs. body-text mismatches regarding `cites_evidence`.\\n2. Search for any \\\"HW-REG-\\\" documents (e.g. HW-REG-open-obligations) and see what registries exist and what they track — report the file paths and a brief description of each registry's purpose and format.\\n3. Check docs/spec/ for any document describing the validation rule for `cites_evidence` (e.g. is there a check that validates that every inline `[evaluation](...)` link in a spec doc body is reflected in cites_evidence front matter, and vice versa?). Look in docs/spec/ (especially the check-layer or decisions or requirements specs) and also check engine/crates/check source if present for a check name like \\\"evidence\\\" or \\\"cites\\\".\\n4.
```
